context.problem_statement: Analyze an A/B test for a new checkout page design. Group A is the control (existing design) and Group B is the treatment (new design). Perform a two-proportion z-test to determine if the conversion rate difference is statistically significant. Compute: (1) conversion rates for each group, (2) absolute lift and relative lift, (3) z-statistic and p-value (two-tailed), (4) 95% confidence interval for the difference in proportions, (5) minimum detectable effect and whether the study was adequately powered (assume 80% power target).
context.expert_knowledge: Two-proportion z-test: z = (p1 - p2) / sqrt(p_pool*(1-p_pool)*(1/n1 + 1/n2)) where p_pool = (x1+x2)/(n1+n2). Use statsmodels.stats.proportion.proportions_ztest. CI for difference: (p1-p2) ± 1.96*sqrt(p1(1-p1)/n1 + p2(1-p2)/n2). Relative lift = (p_treatment - p_control) / p_control. MDE = effect size detectable at given power/alpha.
